mechanism_narrative: The sustained improvement in WORKPLACES mobility over the last two weeks (from -39.7 to -30.9) indicates a return to office-based work, which will directly increase weekday retail and recreation activity in commercial areas, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The recent shift of GROCERY_PHARM mobility to above baseline (+2.0 at t-0w) signifies increased consumer confidence and willingness to engage in out-of-home activities, which will spill over into non-essential retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not show a clear upward trend in the next two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM crosses the baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of high PARKS mobility and declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (from t-3w to t-0w, 10.7 to 8.6) suggests a shift from staying at home to outdoor leisure activities. As people spend more time outside their homes, they are more likely to visit retail and recreation venues, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC decreases over the next four weeks while PARKS remains high and RESIDENTIAL continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, the gradual but consistent improvement in TRANSIT station visits (from -45.1 to -41.7) indicates increasing public transport usage, which facilitates access to urban retail and recreation centers, thereby boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT shows week-on-week improvement for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks despite sustained improvements in TRANSIT mobility during a reopening phase.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from t-3w (10.7) to t-0w (8.6), despite a slight bump at t-1w, indicates a sustained trend of people spending less time at home. This increased out-of-home activity will naturally translate to higher engagement with retail and recreation venues, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The combined strong upward trend in WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM mobility signifies a broad return to daily routines and economic activity. This increased movement for work and essential shopping creates more opportunities and necessity for people to visit retail and recreation establishments, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not improve in the next two weeks despite both WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM showing continued positive trends.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained high level of PARKS mobility (above 40% for the last three weeks) indicates favorable weather conditions and a strong preference for outdoor activities. This general increase in out-of-home movement, especially during leisure time, will eventually translate into higher footfall for nearby retail and recreation businesses, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility remains above 40% for 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC declines in the next week, despite PARKS mobility remaining above 40%.

mechanism_narrative: Despite other categories showing recovery, RETAIL_REC has remained significantly below baseline and flat in recent weeks. This indicates a lagging recovery in discretionary spending and leisure activities. In a slow recovery regime, this inertia suggests RETAIL_REC will continue to stagnate or slightly decline over the next four weeks until a stronger catalyst emerges.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC remains below -30% for 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC shows a significant upward trend (e.g., >5 percentage points) over the next four weeks.
